steps.title: Isolate and Cryopreserve PBMCs
steps.instruction: Dilute 40 mL fresh buffy coat 1:1 with sterile PBS (40 mL). Add 15 mL Ficoll‑Hypaque to each of four 50 mL conical tubes, carefully overlay 20 mL diluted buffy coat onto the Ficoll without mixing. Balance tubes within ±0.2 g and centrifuge 30 min at 400 × g, 20–22 °C, brakes off. Using a transfer pipette, collect cells from the plasma‑Ficoll interface into a new 50 mL tube. Wash twice by topping up to 40 mL with complete RPMI or PBS and centrifuge 10 min at 500 × g. (Optional) Resuspend pellet in 10 mL ACK lysis buffer, incubate 5 min at 20–22 °C, then wash. Resuspend in 30 mL complete RPMI, remove clumps, mix 1:1 with trypan blue (10 µL each), count cells on a hemocytometer and record viability; dilute if density is too high. Centrifuge 10 min at 500 × g, resuspend in freezing media (50 % complete RPMI, 40 % FCS, 10 % DMSO) to a final concentration of 50–100 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹. Quickly aliquot 1 mL into 1.5 mL screw‑top cryotubes, place tubes in a Mr. Frosty container at –80 °C for 18–24 h, then transfer to liquid nitrogen for long‑term storage. Follow institutional biosafety and bioethics regulations.

steps.title: Prepare Complete RPMI/DMEM Media
steps.instruction: Prepare complete RPMI 1640 or DMEM by adding heat‑inactivated 10 % fetal calf serum, 2 mM GlutaMAX, 1 mM sodium pyruvate, 10 mM HEPES, and 1× penicillin/streptomycin. Store at 4 °C and warm to 37 °C in a water bath for 30 min before use.

steps.title: Prepare 1.7 mg/mL Collagen Gel Mix
steps.instruction: On ice, combine the following to obtain 540 µL cell‑collagen mixture (maximum 3 × 10⁶ total cells): 148 µL 3.1 mg/mL bovine pure collagen (final 1.7 mg/mL), 20 µL 10× MEM (0.74×), 10 µL 7.5 % sodium bicarbonate (0.28 % final), 92 µL cell suspension in complete RPMI (up to 1 × 10⁶ cells), and sterile water or additional RPMI to bring the total volume to 540 µL. Keep all components on ice until mixing.

steps.title: Set Up Heating Platform and Temperature Monitoring
steps.instruction: Install the heating platform (Werner Instruments TC344C) with two heating resistors on the metal base. Connect the platform to its temperature controller. Attach a thermocouple thermometer (Cole Parmer #RK‑91210‑30) with Omega probe #5SC‑TT‑K‑40‑72 to continuously monitor the collagen chamber temperature. Adjust the controller to maintain 37 °C throughout the experiment. Humidity or CO₂ control is not required for this setup.

steps.title: Thaw and Activate Naïve CD4⁺ T Cells
steps.instruction: Day 0: Thaw cryopreserved PBMCs in a 37 °C water bath. Add warm complete RPMI to achieve a 1:9 ratio (1 mL cells : 9 mL RPMI) in a 50 mL conical tube. Centrifuge 10 min at 400 × g, 20–22 °C; discard supernatant and resuspend in 10 mL fresh RPMI. Repeat the wash twice. Count cells with trypan blue; viability should be ≥80 %. Resuspend at 50 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ in EasySep buffer and perform negative selection using the EasySep Human Naïve CD4⁺ T‑cell Isolation Kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol. Transfer the selected cells to a 15 mL tube, wash with 5 mL RPMI, count, and resuspend at 1 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ in RPMI. Plate 1 mL per well of a 24‑well plate (1 × 10⁶ cells per well) and add 25 µL anti‑CD3ε/CD28 Dynabeads (1:1 bead‑to‑cell ratio). Mix gently and incubate 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 48 h. Day 2: Transfer the culture to a 5 mL Falcon tube, place in an EasySep magnet for 2 min to capture beads, then decant the bead‑free T cells into a fresh 15 mL tube and wash with 3 mL RPMI. Count cells and dilute to 0.1–0.2 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ in RPMI containing 8 ng mL⁻¹ recombinant human IL‑2; seed in a T25 or T75 flask standing upright. Allow expansion for 3 days without media change. Day 5: Replace media with RPMI + 8 ng mL⁻¹ IL‑2 and adjust the cell density to 1 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹; set the final volume according to experimental needs. Days 6–9: Perform phenotypic flow‑cytometry using fluorochrome‑conjugated anti‑CD3, CD4, CD8, CD62L, CD45RO, and CCR7 to distinguish effector and central memory subsets. Use cells from days 6–9 for downstream imaging and HIV infection experiments.

steps.title: Differentiate Monocyte‑Derived Dendritic Cells
steps.instruction: Day 0: Thaw frozen PBMCs in a 37 °C water bath. Add warm RPMI at a 1:9 ratio (1 mL cells : 9 mL RPMI) in a 50 mL tube. Centrifuge 10 min at 500 × g, 20–22 °C; discard supernatant, add 10 mL fresh RPMI, and repeat the wash twice. Count cells. Resuspend at 100 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ in EasySep buffer and perform positive selection for CD14⁺ monocytes using the EasySep Human CD14 Positive Selection Kit per manufacturer’s instructions. Resuspend monocytes at 1–2 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ in RPMI supplemented with 50 ng mL⁻¹ rhGM‑CSF and 50 ng mL⁻¹ rhIL‑4. Plate in ultra‑low‑attachment Nunc Sphera T25 or T75 flasks and incubate 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Day 2: Collect cells, centrifuge 10 min at 400 × g, resuspend in fresh RPMI + 50 ng mL⁻¹ rhGM‑CSF and 50 ng mL⁻¹ rhIL‑4, maintaining 1–2 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹, and return to the incubator. Day 5: For maturation, resuspend cells at 0.8 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ in RPMI containing 25 ng mL⁻¹ rhGM‑CSF, 25 ng mL⁻¹ rhIL‑4, and 100 ng mL⁻¹ LPS (S. Minnesota); incubate 24 h. Verify maturation by flow cytometry for up‑regulated CD80, CD86, and MHC‑II.

steps.title: Convert and Load Images into Imaris
steps.instruction: Convert the original .xml microscopy files to .ims format using the Imaris FileConverter. Open the .ims files in Imaris 8.2. In Edit → Image Properties, set the minimum X, Y, and Z values to 0, adjust the voxel size for the Z dimension (e.g., 4 µm), and under the Time Point section select “All Equidistant” and set the Time Interval to match the acquisition period; if the image disappears, press “Fit”. Add new Spots (orange circles), specify algorithm parameters, choose a region of interest, select the channel to analyze, and input the approximate XY diameter. Slide the detection‑intensity bar until each spot corresponds to a single cell body. Delete any tracks where the entire cell is not in the field of view via the Edit Tracks tab. Inspect each track for accuracy; manually connect split tracks by selecting Object, then two objects while holding the Ctrl (or Command) key and clicking “Connect”. Perform separate tracking for dendritic cells and T cells. When tracking is finished, open the Statistics tab and export all migration parameters to an Excel file for downstream analysis (e.g., custom MATLAB scripts).

steps.title: Embed Cells in Collagen and Fix
steps.instruction: Prepare 540 µL of cell‑collagen mixture as described in Step 3 (maximum 3 × 10⁶ cells). Dispense the 540 µL suspension into a well of a 24‑well plate to create a cell “bubble”. Incubate at 37 °C until the gel solidifies. Add 2 mL pre‑warmed 4 % paraformaldehyde in 5 % sucrose to each well and incubate 24 h at 37 °C. Remove the PFA solution and wash gently three times with 2 mL PBS + 0.2 % Tween‑20, 5 min per wash, aspirating carefully each time. Add 2 mL 0.15 M glycine buffer (pH 7) to quench excess PFA; place the plate at 4 °C for 18–24 h, ensuring the gels are completely submerged. Rinse three times with PBS + 0.2 % Tween‑20 and aspirate. Permeabilize by adding 2 mL 0.5 % Triton X solution; incubate 48 h at 4 °C. Rinse three times with wash buffer and aspirate. Block non‑specific binding by adding 2 mL 1 % BSA in PBS; incubate 18–24 h at 4 °C. Rinse three times with wash buffer and proceed to staining.

steps.title: Stain Collagen Gels with Phalloidin
steps.instruction: Transfer each gel block to a new 24‑well culture dish using a plastic spoon. Add 300–500 µL of 1.65 µM Texas‑Red‑conjugated phalloidin (prepared according to the manufacturer’s instructions) to fully cover the gel; incubate 24 h at 4 °C in the dark. Rinse the gels three times with wash buffer, 5 min per wash, and gently aspirate. Using a plastic spoon, place each gel onto a glass microscope slide; blot excess liquid with a Kimwipe, leaving the gel in place. Apply vacuum grease (dispensed with a 5 mL syringe) around the gel, matching the grease height to the gel thickness, to create an airtight seal. Add a small volume of PBS into the grease well and gently place a coverslip on top, pressing slightly to seal and eliminate air bubbles; if bubbles remain, inject additional PBS with an insulin syringe. Mount the slides on the microscope and acquire 3‑D image stacks with a z‑spacing of 1–2 µm for reconstruction. Images can be imported into Imaris or ImageJ for further analysis. (Optional: for antibody staining, rinse gels five times, 5 min each, between primary and secondary antibody incubations.)
